cues: Oliver Sacks was born in London in nineteen thirty three, the son of two doctors.
He studied medicine at Oxford and from nineteen sixty five worked as a neurologist in New York for nearly fifty years.
He became famous for writing about his patients as human beings rather than cases, in books like Awakenings.
The New York Times called him the poet laureate of medicine.
This is a personal essay: first person, memories that move towards an opinion.
The textbook calls it a praise of intellectual freedom, community, and the joy of lucky discovery.
